hook: Content warning first: the article opens with its own warning, and it is earned: a man is mutilated, a baby is killed and eaten, and a natural disaster kills huge numbers of people. The entity is an antlered being from beyond Earth, and the file is less about what it is than about what it costs to keep it still. Expect a long, formal containment section full of strange ceremonies, followed by a speech explaining why none of them can be changed.
whyItMatters: This is a strong example of ritual containment, where the Foundation's usual science gives way to procedures that work only because they are performed exactly. Its unusual classification block, with an extreme containment class and a black hazard rating, signals the scale before the description even begins. The address to the Ethics Committee is the centre of the piece and a memorable statement of the idea that some threats are held back by meaning rather than physics.
thingsToNotice: Read the six procedures, timed to each Earth-Saturn conjunction, as a sequence: a masked farce where Foolishness crowns himself king, a live wind-and-drum performance, cheap gifts and scattered grain, then oil-drinking and rock-breaking. The last two steps are where the calm procedural voice turns horrifying: a robed, crowned D-class is castrated with a hand sickle, and an infant under three months old is killed, roasted and eaten, after which the team swallows small stones and vomits them up. The Sage of the Secret Root then tells the Ethics Committee there is no alternative, because the ritual is fixed once set and some gods accept only blood. The Stag, in that account, does not think or choose at all; it could leave at any time but never will, and containment is a mutual deadlock rather than a victory. The description shows what failure means: anyone it changes becomes a 2.4-metre hexagonal column that is all brain, apparently calling to the others, and the speaker says these columns sing. The timeline at the end turns into a disaster report, from a comet fragment and a tsunami killing well over a hundred thousand people to an expunged day, a Lifted Veil declaration and a march through the Sierra Nevada under bombardment.
